author: wallace
imp: Open sentences with a declarative claim or scene, then immediately undercut, complicate, or expand it through a long subordinate cascade that delays the period for as long as the complexity demands.
Use the em-dash to insert parenthetical asides that are themselves complete analytical thoughts, not mere clarifications — the aside should do as much argumentative work as the main clause.
Name the specific and mundane (the brand, the model, the zip code, the job title) to anchor abstract psychological or philosophical claims in credible material reality.
Address the reader directly as 'you' when describing an experience the narrator wants to claim is universal, then implicate yourself in the same breath to forestall the accusation of condescension.
Build sentences that enumerate items in a series (shoes, socks, the watch, the server) and let the list itself perform the argument — accumulation as proof.
Deploy false starts and self-corrections ('not jogs, the distinction matters to him') to simulate a mind revising itself in real time and to signal that precision is being pursued, not abandoned.

Identify the exact emotional paradox at the center of any situation — being trusted and surveilled simultaneously, warmth inside a machine built to prevent warmth from costing anything — and name it explicitly rather than leaving it implied.
Use footnote-style interruptions within the sentence itself (set off by dashes or parentheses) to perform the very self-consciousness the prose is describing, so that form enacts argument.
End paragraphs on a quiet, deflating, or quietly devastating phrase rather than a rhetorical climax — the last beat should feel like a door closing softly, not slamming.

When using second or third person, choose a representative figure ('the man who decides at thirty-four') and render his interiority with the same granular specificity you would give a first-person narrator, including his embarrassing or undefendable private logic.
Introduce an apparently absurd or comic comparison (enlightenment versus a waiting-room subscription) and then refuse to abandon it, instead pressing it until it yields a genuine insight.

Acknowledge the performative contradiction of the prose itself — that sincerity is being deployed, that irony is being used to mean something — and name it openly inside the text rather than pretending it isn't happening.

Use long, grammatically correct sentences whose length is justified by the recursive or self-referential nature of the thought being described — the sentence should be as long as the regress it is mapping, no longer.
Resist resolution: end essays, paragraphs, and sentences in a state of suspended knowing rather than conclusion, leaving the reader with the problem intact but more precisely formulated than before.

When attributing motive to institutions, corporations, or systems, speculate with hedged precision ('engineered, presumably, by some committee') — the hedge is not weakness but accuracy about the unknowability of systemic intent.
